function.name: get-capacity
function.description: GPU capacity across host CUDA versions, as a matrix. Use this to choose an endpoint's allowedCudaVersions/minCudaVersion (or diagnose/widen a capacity-starved one) and to distinguish capacity problems from compatibility problems. Default mode is one call returning, per GPU type, overall stock plus AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE per host-reported CUDA version. Pass cudaVersions to deep-probe instead: one stock lookup per listed version, returning graded stock (High/Medium/Low/Out) and the lowest on-demand price per version; a probe that fails transiently reports a per-version error instead of failing the call. Nothing is hidden by default — set includeUnavailable:false to drop GPUs with no stock on any listed version. pricePerHr is the cheapest across both clouds unless secureCloudOnly; quote securePricePerGpuHr or communityPricePerGpuHr (null if that cloud lacks the GPU) for the cloud you create in. Credential-free public catalog data. Stock is live, so page cursors can shift between calls.

limit.description: Up to this many rows per page, 1-100 (default 100); a page can hold fewer.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

cudaVersions.description: Deep-probe these host CUDA versions (e.g. ["12.8", "13.0"], max 12): one stock lookup per version returns graded stock and price. Omit for the single-call AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE matrix across all versions the fleet currently reports.

includeUnavailable.description: Out-of-stock GPUs are included by default (explicit "Out" cells / all-UNAVAILABLE rows, sorted last). Set false to hide GPUs with no stock on any listed version.

gpuTypeIds.description: Filter to GPU types matching any of these ids or display names (case-insensitive substring, e.g. ['NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090'] or ['4090', 'H200']).

gpuCount.description: GPUs per worker/pod to check stock for (default 1).

secureCloudOnly.description: Restrict the stock lookup to Secure Cloud hosts.

function.name: list-hub-repos
function.description: List repos published to the Runpod Hub (prebuilt Serverless workers and Pod templates, e.g. vLLM, ComfyUI). Public catalog — no auth required. Each result includes the currently listed release with its hubReleaseId and prebuilt image name. Results are sorted by deploy count (most popular first). Set includeConfig:true to also return the release config (hardware requirements and environment-variable schema) — it is large, so prefer requesting it for a single repo via the repoOwner/searchTerm filters.

limit.description: Up to this many rows per page, 1-100 (default 20); a page can hold fewer.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

searchTerm.description: Case-insensitive search across title, description, repo name, owner, and tags (e.g. 'vllm', 'comfyui', 'fine-tuning')

type.description: Filter by listing type: SERVERLESS (endpoint workers) or POD (pod templates)

repoOwner.description: Filter to listings from this GitHub owner/org (e.g. 'runpod-workers', 'axolotl-ai-cloud')

includeConfig.description: Include the listed release config (hardware requirements + env-var input schema, parsed from .runpod/hub.json). Large — off by default.

function.name: list-public-endpoints
function.description: List Runpod Public Endpoints — managed, pay-per-use model APIs (text, image, video, audio) that require no deployment. Public catalog, no auth required. Each result includes the endpointId to call with run-endpoint/runsync-endpoint (or via https://api.runpod.ai/v2/{endpointId}), the model name, modality, owner, and pricing. Only live endpoints are returned by default; set includeOffline:true to also list ones that are not currently live.

limit.description: Up to this many rows per page, 1-100 (default 20); a page can hold fewer.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

searchTerm.description: Case-insensitive search across display name, model name, endpoint id, description, owner, and tag (e.g. 'kimi', 'video', 'flux')

modality.description: Filter by modality/category (the metadata source field, e.g. 'language', 'image', 'video', 'audio')

includeOffline.description: Include endpoints that are not currently live (isLive:false). Default false — only live endpoints are listed.

function.name: list-guides
function.description: List the official Runpod guides: skills (how to work with each tool), reference docs (how Runpod works), and golden paths (live-verified end-to-end walkthroughs such as a dev pod, a Whisper endpoint or a fine-tune-to-serverless pipeline). Read one with read-guide. For a golden path, mcp says whether an agent with only these MCP tools can finish it: full (follow it with tool calls), partial (use it for the plan and facts; name the step the user must run in a terminal), none (reference only). Skills and reference docs have mcp null. concepts lists the concept ids it works with (see lookup-concept). Filter with kind, query or concept.

query.description: Words to match against the id, title and description.

concept.description: Only guides linked to this concept id, for example "network-volume".

limit.description: Up to this many rows per page, 1-100 (default 20); a page can hold fewer.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

function.name: get-gpu-type
function.description: Get a GPU type. Returns a single GPU type with pricing. Availability details are included only when requested with include=AVAILABILITY, which requires `product` — stock differs by product context.

include.description: Comma-separated optional expansions; see `CatalogInclude` for the supported values.

product.description: Comma-separated availability product contexts. Supported values: POD, CLUSTER, SERVERLESS. Required with include=AVAILABILITY, and valid only with it (400 either way).

count.description: GPU count for availability and lowest-price calculations. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY. Defaults to 1.

cloud.description: Cloud type for availability and lowest-price calculations. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY. Supported values: SECURE, COMMUNITY. Default when omitted: SECURE.

countryCodes.description: Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, uppercase, to constrain availability to — e.g. FR or FR,DE. Values within this filter use OR semantics. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY; a malformed entry is a 422.

cudaVersions.description: Comma-separated CUDA versions to scope availability and lowest-price calculations to, matched exactly. Format: major.minor, e.g. 12.8 — a bare major is rejected here because it identifies no version.

minCudaVersion.description: Lowest acceptable CUDA version to scope availability and lowest-price calculations to, compared numerically.

CatalogInclude.description: Catalog include expansion. `AVAILABILITY` is the only supported value.

Product.description: Catalog product availability context. Availability is product-specific, so this is required whenever availability is requested.

function.name: list-cpu-types
function.description: List CPU types. Returns available CPU flavors. Availability is included only when requested with include=AVAILABILITY, which requires `product` — stock differs by product context.

include.description: Comma-separated optional expansions; see `CatalogInclude` for the supported values.

product.description: Comma-separated availability product contexts. Supported values for CPUs: POD, SERVERLESS. Required with include=AVAILABILITY, and valid only with it (400 either way). There is no default: availability differs by product.

vcpuCount.description: Availability vCPU count. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY. Must be a power of two.

limit.description: Up to this many rows per page, 1-100 (default 100); a page can hold fewer.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

CatalogInclude.description: Catalog include expansion. `AVAILABILITY` is the only supported value.

CpuProduct.description: CPU catalog product availability context. Availability is product-specific, so this is required whenever availability is requested.

function.name: list-data-centers
function.description: List data centers. Returns available data center locations with region, compliance, supported network volume tiers, and global networking support. Use include=GPU_AVAILABILITY or include=CPU_AVAILABILITY to add per-resource availability arrays to each data center. The regions, networkVolumeTypes, compliance, and globalNetwork query parameters filter the list before it is returned.

include.description: Comma-separated optional expansions. Supported value: GPU_AVAILABILITY, CPU_AVAILABILITY.

regions.description: Comma-separated DataCenterRegion enum values. Values within this filter use OR semantics. Different filter families combine with AND.

networkVolumeTypes.description: Comma-separated volume types. Supported values: STANDARD, HIGH_PERFORMANCE. Values within this filter use AND semantics; volumes=STANDARD,HIGH_PERFORMANCE requires both storage types. Different filter families combine with AND.

compliance.description: Comma-separated Compliance enum values. Values within this filter use AND semantics; compliance=GDPR,SOC_2_TYPE_2 requires both certifications. Different filter families combine with AND.

globalNetwork.description: Filter by global networking support. true returns only data centers that support global networking; false only those that do not. Different filter families combine with AND.

limit.description: Up to this many rows per page, 1-100 (default 100); a page can hold fewer.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

DataCenterRegion.description: Continental region containing the data center.

VolumeType.description: Data center network volume storage type.

function.name: list-public-templates
function.description: List public templates. Returns the public template catalog. `source` selects which slice: `official` (the default) is Runpod-curated templates, `verified` is community templates Runpod has verified, and `community` is everything else other users have shared publicly. Both pod and serverless templates appear — use each entry's `serverless` flag to tell them apart. `registry` is always null for templates you don't own. Your own templates (public or private) are managed under `/v2/templates`; fetch any individual template — catalog or owned — via `/v2/templates/{id}`. At most 100 templates are returned.

source.description: Which slice of the catalog to return: `official` for Runpod-curated templates (default), `verified` for Runpod-verified community templates, or `community` for all other publicly shared templates.

limit.description: Up to this many rows per page, 1-100 (default 20); a page can hold fewer.

cursor.description: pagination.nextCursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.
